questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to live in the U.S. and experience the country - another crucial aspect was I wanted to improve my english skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult. It takes a lot of work to figure out everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person who took care of all the the exchange students. All of the exchange students lived in a hotel in Boston. There were some other students from the University who were employed to help us. The hotel had an office where we could get all the help we needed from them. That was very nice to know, that we could get help and go ask people if that was necessary.

questions.answer: I think it was fine. Its your responsibility to keep up with deadlines, but if you join the few meetings the host university offers, then you should be fine.

questions.answer: Meetings and an exchange office we could reach out to through email and phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A bit complicated, but every new system is complicated in the beginning.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
It was fine. I think its easier to get a better grade in the U.S compared to Denmark. In Denmark its only the final exam your grades depend on. In the U.S., things such as participation, assignments, quizzes, midterms, final exam ect. But they really expect you to show up; otherwise, it will be at the expense of your grade. 
It depends on the course, but I think the level in general is very similar to Denmark.
